rows.52:03c8:
I'm Makoto Shindo.
Third-year.
The seventh one sure is late...
Seriously, what's the hold-up...
Well, whatever.{p}If you don't end up with a full set of stories, it's not like I'm the one who's stuck.
rows.52:04a4:
Don't get all huffy, {a}.
I think you're cuter when you smile.{p}
rows.52:0548:
Anyway, none of that matters.
All right, listen to my story.
This is about a strange dream I had.
No, maybe I'm the only one who thinks it was a dream, and it was actually real.
Either way, it was one hell of a terrifying dream.{p}
rows.52:063c:
In the dream...
I'm out in the school's back courtyard, beating the hell out of some guy.
Punching, kicking, anything goes.
The guy just takes it and doesn't fight back at all.
Even when he's covered in bruises, even when his face swells up, he doesn't fight back. He doesn't even let out a single scream.{p}
rows.52:073c:
Only a coward beats on someone who won't fight back, right?
I can't stand guys like that.
So even if it's just a dream, if I caught myself pulling something that low, I ought to be furious with myself.
But you know...
After I have this dream, I just feel great.
All the worries and irritation that had been knotted up inside me vanish, clean gone, and my body feels lighter somehow.
Come to think of it, I only ever have this dream when I'm fed up and pissed off.
I guess it's some kind of stress relief.
Every time I had this dream, I'd get this rush I can't even describe, and then feel just a little twinge of bitter guilt.
And the violence, like some kind of bullying, went on and on in my dreams.
Then, one day...{p}
rows.52:09e4:
I finally killed the guy.
I was beating on him like always, when all of a sudden he toppled over onto the ground.
He lay on his back, blood trickling from his mouth...
It was a face I'd never seen before.
The red blood spread out across the ground......
"...Guess he's dead."
I think I muttered something like that.{p}
rows.52:0b30:
After that, I never had the dream again...
But you know, that's what makes it scarier.
I can't shake the feeling that I really did kill that guy.
The color of the blood pouring out of his body back then, that's the one thing that feels weirdly vivid...
Even if it only happened in a dream, it still leaves a bad taste in your mouth, right?
So I figured I'd try reading one of those dream-interpretation books.
I thought if I could slap some kind of logical-sounding analysis on this dream of mine, anything at all, I might settle down a little.
There's someone like that in my class.
Someone who's into that kind of stuff.{p}
rows.52:0d24: Hey, {a}.{p}You like fortune-telling and stuff too, right?
rows.52:0d7c:
Ha ha ha... I knew it.
I figured you would.
Me, I'm not the type who believes in fortune-telling.
That was the first time I'd ever read a book like that.{p}
rows.52:0e14:
There was even an entry for dreams about killing.
...If it's in there, that means other people have dreams about killing too, right?
Well, not that it matters...
I was surprised when I read that page.
Dreams about killing are......{p}
rows.52:0f48: A dream neither good nor bad
rows.52:0fbc:
A dream that signifies rising fortunes; all sorts of things will be on the upswing and go well.
...That's what it said.
It kind of surprised me.
I felt totally deflated.
All my worrying up till then started to seem kind of stupid.{p}
rows.52:1088:
You said earlier you liked fortune-telling and stuff, right?
Then you must've tried all kinds of fortunes.
I bet you've been let down by the results once or twice, haven't you?
It wasn't a bad result, but somehow I couldn't bring myself to just swallow it whole and accept it.
For once I'd started thinking I might try believing in fortune-telling, but when it was written that breezily, I just ended up disappointed.
It was a mistake to look for an explanation of that dream in a passage only a few lines long.
If I'd read some thick book written by a psychologist or a philosopher, I probably would've found a better answer, but...
I'm not really much for reading books.
In the end, I just told myself,
"It only happened in a dream..."
and with that one phrase, I decided to write the whole thing off.
And I thought I'd forgotten all about the dream, clean and completely, but...
Today, coming here, it suddenly came back to me.
And the reason why is......{p}
rows.52:13b0:
...Whoa, a blackout?
Great.
Can't see a damn thing like this.
Well, it doesn't really matter for telling the story...
What do you want to do, {a}?{p}Are you okay with me just carrying on like this?
rows.52:1454: Let's go on with the story
rows.52:1468: Let's take a break for now
rows.52:14ac:
"Let's go on with the story."
I said it firmly.
Scary stories are so much more exciting when you hear them in the dark.
Besides...
If the seventh one doesn't come, Shindo's story is the last.
If it'll all be over in just a little while, I want to finish the interview properly.
...That's what I thought.{p}
rows.52:159c:
But just then...
"Gah!"
Suddenly, there was a short scream.
It was Shindo's voice.
It was pitch-black; I couldn't tell what had happened.
"Shindo...★"{p}
rows.52:16a4:
The darkness before my eyes twisted violently and began to form an eerie whirlpool.
And my consciousness was dragged down in one rush, deeper still into the depths of the darkness...{p}
rows.52:1738:
Ha ha ha...
Getting defiant on me now?{p}
rows.52:1770:
Then don't make such a worried face.
You're cute when you smile, you know.{p}
rows.52:17cc:
...{a}.
You're in high school now, so don't cry over something like this.
If you keep crying like that, you'll ruin that cute face of yours.
You're way cuter when you're smiling.{p}
rows.52:187c:
You don't...?
Well, that's a surprise.
I mean, I figured anyone who'd come to cover something like a seven-wonders feature would be into fortune-telling and stuff.
I'm not the type who believes in fortune-telling either.
That was the first time I'd ever read a book like that.{p}
rows.52:1954:
...You think so too?
Actually, that's what I thought too.
Killing someone just feels kind of ominous, right?
I was getting a little uneasy, wondering if it was an omen that something bad was about to happen.
But you know...
What the book said was the total opposite of what I'd imagined.
Turns out a dream about killing is a good dream.{p}
rows.52:1a80:
Most people would think so.
I did too.
You know how they say dreams show what's in your unconscious, right?
I couldn't help being scared of myself, wondering if deep down, without knowing it, I wanted to kill somebody.
But you know, what the book said was the total opposite.
Turns out a dream about killing is a good dream.{p}
rows.52:1c4c:
"Should we take a break for now?"
I asked timidly.
I don't have the nerve to listen to scary stories in pitch darkness like this.
If we stop for a bit, I'm sure the lights will come back on before long...
But then...
"Listen.
I'd like to go home soon.
If we aren't continuing the story, then I'll be taking my leave."
That sullen voice must be Iwashita.
I can't see her in the dark, but I feel like I can almost see an aura of anger around where she's sitting...{p}...What should I do?
rows.52:1e1c:
"All right.
Let's go on with the story."
I said it firmly.
If the seventh one doesn't come, Shindo's story is the last.
Rather than leave the interview half-finished, I want to see it through to the end.
...That's what I thought.{p}
rows.52:1ed4:
"Then let's end it here."
Shindo's story seemed to be mostly over, and there was no sign of the seventh one showing up.
In that case, I don't think there's any problem with wrapping things up here.
Then Shindo spoke up, sounding displeased.
"Come on, {a}.
So you won't hear my story out to the end, huh?
And we were just getting to the important part..."
With that, Shindo fell silent.
What should I do...
I think I hurt his feelings.
Maybe I should apologize...
rows.52:20ac:
"Gyaaaaaagh☆"
A piercing scream rang out from the darkness.
Whose voice was that...★
It was pitch-black; I couldn't tell what had happened.
And then again...
rows.52:213c:
"Eeeeeeek☆"
This time, a woman's shrill scream...
...Fukuzawa?
Or Iwashita...?
rows.52:21cc:
"Waaaaaagh!"
Scream after scream rang out before I even had time to think.
What...?
What's happening?
I asked desperately, but the darkness spreading before my eyes gave me no answer.
And then...
rows.52:2344:
"Hh...☆"
I looked around the room and gasped.
Under the lights, the floor and the walls were stained bright red.
Here and there lay the members, collapsed...
Arai was by the wall, and Fukuzawa lay beside him.
The one sprawled on the floor, chair and all, was Kazama.
Hosoda had died in his seat, and Iwashita had died reaching for the door.
And in front of the door...{p}
rows.52:24a8:
Standing there, drenched in red, was Shindo.
"Shindo...?"
At first I thought he was dead.
But Shindo was breathing hard, his shoulders heaving.
Looking closer, all the blood on him seemed to be someone else's...
...Which means Shindo was the one who killed the other five★{p}
rows.52:25b8:
His eyes glittering, Shindo walked toward me.
"What's wrong, {a}?
Why so scared-looking...
Are you afraid of me?
Ha ha ha...
Sure, I'm the one who killed these guys.
But you know...
There's someone way scarier than me.
And that's... Hino.
Hino's a scary guy.
We barely know each other, and before I knew it, he'd seen right through to the real me.
{a}...
Want me to let you in on something good?
Hino's planning to write an article that'll blow everyone away.
A horrifyingly shocking article about a newspaper club member who was covering the seven wonders in the school after hours, got caught up in a gruesome incident, and died along with the whole group...
Surprised?
This is the guy who built the newspaper club up from a nobody club into what it is now.
He'd pull off something like that without batting an eye.
Ha ha ha...
Well, none of that matters to me.
As long as I get to kill you all, I'm happy.
I love beating defenseless people to death, nice and slow."{p}
rows.52:2990:
"Shindo...
What on earth happened to you?"
"Bwa-ha-ha-ha-ha-ha...
Now that you mention it, that was the name of this body's original owner.
That guy called Shindo got swallowed up by the cruelty lurking in his own heart.
In the dream, when he killed that man.
From that moment on, I've been Makoto Shindo.
Too bad, huh?
All that interviewing, and now you'll never get to write your article...
Frustrating, isn't it?
Yes, yes, that's the face I love.
Shindo said he liked your smile, but me, what I like best of all is that face of yours, all twisted up with frustration and despair.
It's the moment you feel most keenly what tiny, foolish creatures humans are."{p}
rows.52:2bd8:
Sad and frustrated... I felt the tears welling up.
Even knowing it would only delight that thing, I just couldn't stop them.{p}
rows.52:2c5c:
"Oops, it's almost time for Hino to show up.
It's a shame to go, but I think I'll take my leave now.
rows.52:2cc4: With that, 'it', wearing Shindo's form, smashed the windowpane.{p}
rows.52:2d18: The shards raining down, glittering as they caught the light, were beautiful.{p}
rows.52:2d70:
'It' picked up a clear shard and slowly came toward me.
I have to run...
My mind knew it, but my body wouldn't obey.
Like a frog glared at by a snake, all I could do was tremble and shake...
...Oh, it's over!
The glass shard was thrust out in front of my eyes.
And then...{p}
rows.52:2e84:
"So long, {a}."
The arm gripping it moved swiftly.{p}
rows.52:2ed0:
For an instant, something hot ran across my neck.
A moment later, something warm began to flow out.
All the strength drained from my body at once...
...Slump.
My body crumpled limply into the pool of blood.
In my vision, slowly turning red...
'It' leapt nimbly onto the window frame and vanished into the darkness outside.{p}
rows.52:3000:
...Click.
For an instant, a white light flooded everything around me.
"Hyah-ha-ha-ha...
Amazing, this is a real scoop!"
Before I knew it, Hino had appeared and was gleefully snapping the shutter.
...Maybe Hino had been swallowed up by the cruelty deep in his heart too.
As my consciousness slipped away, that's what I was thinking.
All that surrounded me was the sharp light of the flash and the shrill laughter pouring from Hino's mouth...{p}
rows.52:3184:
You said earlier you didn't like fortune-telling, right?
Me neither.
Why did I even think of looking for an explanation of the dream in something like that...
It must've really been bugging me.
That's the only way I can see it.
But, you know...
Well, how should I put it... seeing that fortune, I felt like I got past something.
In the end, it was just something that happened in a dream.{p}
rows.52:32cc:
...The moment Shindo said that.
I felt the air in the room stir, as if something rippled through it.
"There was no need to worry about it that much.
It was only a dream, after all."
Hasn't Shindo noticed?
Everyone's eyes are fixed on him...
Every time Shindo says
"Because it was a dream..."
or
"Just a dream..."
everyone's expressions get grimmer...
What should I do...
Maybe I should stop him.
"Um, Shin..."
Just as I started to say it.{p}
rows.52:34bc:
With a tremendous crackling snap, the lights in the room went out.
...A blackout?
"Whoa, a blackout?
Great.
Can't see a damn thing like this.
...Hey, what are you doing?
Hey, cut it out!"
Shindo's voice had clearly turned angry.
And then,
"Gah!"
a short scream rang out.
It was pitch-black; I couldn't tell what had happened.
"Shindo...★"{p}
rows.52:367c:
The darkness before my eyes twisted violently and began to form an eerie whirlpool.
And my consciousness was dragged down in one rush, deeper still into the depths of the darkness...{p}

notes: ★/☆ kept in place as in the source (they seem to stand for ?!/! marks); 52:24a8 and 52:20ac end with ★ in place of a question mark.
